feed.title: Aggregated External AI & Tech News
feed.subtitle: Merged headlines from configured external sources

entry.title: PeopleSoft 0-day affecting hundreds of organizations steals gigabytes of data (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
entry.summary: Vulnerability in the Oracle-owned PeopleSoft software is about as critical as they come.

entry.title: Locked in heated rivalry with researcher, Microsoft fixes 0-day they disclosed (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
entry.summary: A separate zero-day also disclosed by Nightmare Eclipse appears to be patched as well.

entry.title: High-severity vulnerability in Linux caused by a single faulty character (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
entry.summary: Use-after-free bug can be exploited to evade sandbox defenses.

entry.title: For the 2nd time in weeks, Microsoft packages laced with credential stealer (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
entry.summary: 73 packages run self-replicating stealer as soon as they're opened by an AI agent.

entry.title: How a USB-connected speaker can infect a PC without ever being touched (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
entry.summary: Seller of the Sound Blaster Katana V2X doesn't consider the behavior a vulnerability.

entry.title: Dashlane explains how attackers managed to download encrypted password vaults (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
entry.summary: By targeting large numbers of users, attackers increased their chances of success.

entry.title: Can't make sense of Dashlane's vault theft notification? You're not alone. (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
entry.summary: Security advisory leaves out key details. Dashlane maintains complete silence.

entry.title: Dozens of Red Hat packages backdoored through its official NPM channel (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
entry.summary: Anyone who has downloaded affected Red Hat packages should investigate immediately.

entry.title: Botnet of more than 17 million devices dismantled (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
entry.summary: The botnet was reportedly tied to a Russia-based residential proxy network.

entry.title: Fed up with vibe coders, dev sneaks data-nuking prompt injection into their code (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
entry.summary: Undisclosed addition in jqwik instructed AI coding agents to delete app output.

entry.title: Websites have a new way to spy on visitors: Analyzing their SSD activity (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
entry.summary: Telltale SSD activity can be measured in the browser using simple JavaScript.

entry.title: Millions of AI agents imperiled by critical vulnerability in open source package (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
entry.summary: "BadHost" was found in Starlette, a package with 325 million weekly downloads.

entry.title: US's big bet on quantum computing may not be entirely legal (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
entry.summary: Deal also launched the first quantum foundry company, but is there a need for it?

entry.title: Texas AG sues Meta over claims that WhatsApp doesn't provide end-to-end encryption (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
entry.summary: Critics note a lack of factual support in lawsuit filed by US Senate candidate.

entry.title: A hacker group is poisoning open source code at an unprecedented scale (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
entry.summary: GitHub is just the latest victim of TeamPCP, a gang that has carried out a spree of software supply chain attacks.

entry.title: US government takes $2 billion equity stake in nine quantum computing firms (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
entry.summary: Beneficiaries include startup backed by firm with links to the Trump family.

entry.title: Google publishes exploit code threatening millions of Chromium users (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
entry.summary: Google publishes exploit code before patch, reported 42 months earlier, is fixed.

entry.title: In stunning display of stupid, secret CISA credentials found in public GitHub repo (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
entry.summary: SSH keys, plaintext passwords, other sensitive data had been up since November 2025.

entry.title: Zero-day exploit completely defeats default Windows 11 BitLocker protections (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
entry.summary: It's not entirely clear how the exploit works. Microsoft says it's investigating.

entry.title: Cisco announces record revenue and 4,000 layoffs in the same day (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
entry.summary: Layoffs are "not a savings-driven restructure," CFO says.
